The substantive problem is confusing kings with the separately listed clan leaders. The three-sentence minimum is an additional editorial requirement.
Name Joseph and the two officials, and add the failure of Pharaoh’s advisers to explain why the cupbearer speaks. That would also help meet the three-sentence requirement.

JPS uses “descendants of Zilpah,” which accurately covers everyone listed. www.sefaria.org
Required fix: Replace “children and grandchildren” with “descendants.” Zilpah’s servant status is supported by Genesis 29:24. www.chabad.org
“Those” is clear alongside the family list; for a standalone

- “Organized as army units” is supported. Hebrew עַל־צִבְאֹתָם (al tzivotam) refers to their hosts or divisions. JPS renders it “troop by troop.” It need not imply a trained, equipped army. The Sefaria Library
- “I am not a good speaker” is broadly reasonable but imprecise. Hebrew עֲרַל שְׂפָתַיִם (aral sefatayim), literally “uncircumcised of lips,” describes difficulty speaking. JPS uses “tongue-tied”; Rashi explains it as obstructed lips. The verse does not establish a specific diagnosis. The

I checked the Hebrew and Jewish translations. The excerpt omits the frogs entirely, so it does not adequately summarise this episode.
- The central sequence is missing: frogs overrun Egypt; Pharaoh promises to release the people if the frogs are removed; Moses prays; relief comes; Pharaoh then hardens his heart. Bible
- The final sentence is broadly accurate but loses a crucial detail: Pharaoh refuses after receiving relief, breaking his promise. Hebrew וְהַכְבֵּד אֶת־לִבּוֹ describes his harden

The excerpt joins two unrelated laws without explaining the transition.
- “Throw it” has no clear referent. It means meat from an animal torn by beasts, which Israelites were forbidden to eat. It has no connection to the preceding marriage law. This missing context is the biggest problem. The Sefaria Library
- “Tricks” is too specific. Hebrew יְפַתֶּה (yefatteh) is rendered “seduces” by JPS; Rashi explains persuasion or enticement. Deception is not explicitly required by the wording. The Sefaria

note:
The meaning is sound, but Joseph’s example is too vague.
- “Because he trusted God” reasonably expresses πίστει (pistei), “by faith,” which introduces each example.
- Isaac and Jacob’s blessings are accurately described. Joseph’s two sons were Ephraim and Manasseh; “his son” correctly clarifies Joseph’s relationship to Jacob. Bible Gateway
- “Joseph’s prophecy and command” needs explaining. He anticipated the Israelites’ departure from Egypt and instructed them to carry his bones with them. Gene
'They' should be the named tribal leaders, appointed to help Moses and Aaron with the census.
Explain the division: Aaron and his sons cover the holy things; the Kohathites carry them without touching. Sanctuary-entry wording obscures it.
'That area' should be the land of Canaan; nine and a half tribes west of the Jordan, the others already east.
Name the forbidden practices: divination, sorcery, consulting the dead, child sacrifice. 'Disgusting things' and 'that' leave it unexplained.
Twenty verses of war laws: include exemptions, approaching cities, protecting fruit trees.
Include the brother's marriage duty and the public refusal; 'same property' too specific; range also holds a separate law (vv.11–12).
Sentence is about Levi, not Manasseh. Summarise eastern Manasseh's territory, then Levi's inheritance separately.
Stray '}'. Prefer 'Joshua cast lots before the LORD at Shiloh' to 'while Yahweh was watching'. Otherwise good.
flags: g: implied-words brace closed before it opens (UST 18:10)

note: Naming Joshua's father isn't a summary of his death: 110 years, burial, Israel served the LORD in his generation.
Introduce Abimelech, Gaal's rebellion, the attack on Shechem; the stronghold burned with the people sheltering in it.
Wrong referent from joining: Solomon sends Adonijah home, not Joab. Include Adonijah's fear, the altar, Solomon's conditional assurance.
Restore the condition of obedience; the promise is to dwell among Israel, 'in it' narrows it.
Name Ahab and his humbling before God; judgment postponed to his son's days, not cancelled.
Second 'there' is Gibeon, not Ornan's threshing floor. Include the purchase, sacrifice and God's answer; David's fear of Gibeon separately.
Include David's charge to Solomon, obedience, the leaders' help. Heading 'Solomon Anointed' is wrong: no anointing here.
Include Hezekiah's death and burial; range runs through Manasseh's idolatry (33:9): fix the boundary or broaden.
A partial list, not a summary: the returning families and temple staff, total 42,360; not every designation is a town.
Say what the archive search found and what Darius ordered: allow, fund and supply the rebuilding. 'I make this decree' has no substance.
Hebrew 'aph' is anger here, not nose. Central action: fasting and seeking protection, God answered.
Nehemiah declined the governor's allowance and fed others at his own cost; 'do this' should be his prayer to be remembered.
Not only priests: Nehemiah, Levites and leaders sealed the covenant. Summarise the groups, not one group's names.
Too broad: the Ammonite and Moabite restriction and the separation that followed; not a general deportation.
Restore Job's lament: suffering, humiliation, unanswered cries, joy reversed; 'If you came now' obscures music turned to mourning.
Omits the conclusion: enjoying food, drink and work is God's gift.
Assyria as God's instrument, then its arrogance and punishment; keep the wasting and burning imagery.
Punctuation; restore the turn: complacency, devastation, then renewal when the Spirit is poured out.

'Who has believed our report?' is rhetorical. Keep the contrast between the speakers' misjudgment and the servant suffering for others. 'No descendants' is interpretive; readings of servant and speakers differ.
Shorten the long conditional; include inward repentance (heart imagery) and the judgment warning (vv.3–4).
Substitutes Jeremiah's commissioning for the passage: God reveals the plot against Jeremiah; judgment on the men of Anathoth.
Hebrew makes God the subject of dashing them together, parents and children; 'Parents will bash their children' changes the actor.
State the restoration promise and its comparison with the exodus; include the judgment and the nations knowing God.
Add the royal consequence: none of Coniah's offspring will prosper on David's throne.
Include seventy years serving Babylon, then judgment on Babylon; the selection stops before the prophecy's substance.
Says who the letter is to, not its message: settle in Babylon, seek the city's welfare, reject false promises, return after seventy years.
Joining confuses Judah's refugees with the forces in the prophecy: Johanan takes the people to Egypt; the attack is Nebuchadnezzar's invasion.
Name Ezekiel's temple vision and the north gate: matching design, seven steps, a hundred cubits between gates.
Name the south gate: matching dimensions, seven steps, a hundred cubits to the inner gate.
Explain 'those cups': the sacred vessels from the Jerusalem temple, used while praising idols.
Restore the story: Daniel keeps praying, is thrown to the lions, an angel saves him; text jumps from prayer to the accusers' punishment.
Neither sentence explains it: oppressing the poor, disasters without repentance, prepare to meet your God.
Two sentences repeat the question's background; include God's answer: justice, mercy, care for the vulnerable, past disobedience.
State Herod's order to kill the boys around Bethlehem; Rachel's weeping as Matthew's use of Jeremiah, not a genealogy.
Give the conclusion: whoever does my Father's will is my family. Remove 'younger', not stated.
peirazontes means testing, not investigating; include the sign from heaven and the sign of Jonah.
Introduce the man whose house is used; keep to the preparations, the meal starts after the passage.
The tax question, Caesar's image on the coin, render to Caesar and to God: the exchange is missing.
Name Theophilus and the purpose: an investigated, orderly account for certainty about what he was taught.
Name the scribes and Jesus as speaker; their exploiting widows and greater condemnation, not only display.
Remove 'took turns' (unsupported); include the taunt 'who struck you?'. Heading 'The Guards Mock Jesus'.
'Some of them' reads as the believers mocking. Include the Spirit's coming, other languages, the crowd's responses.
Name Saul: told of a plot, his disciples lower him in a basket through the wall at night.
Stray '}'; the Pharisees are believers; include Peter's appeal to grace and James's proposal for Gentiles; explain 'these things'.

note: Joining blurs Paul's warning with the centurion's later orders; include the shipwreck and everyone reaching land.
Restore the doxology: praise to God through Jesus Christ, the revealed mystery, proclaimed to the nations; 'May it be so' has no object.
Include the churches' greetings, Paul's own hand, grace and love at the close; Aquila and Priscilla alone is partial.
Dangling 'Instead'; include grace and peace and Christ giving himself for our sins, with Paul's commission.
Add the apostles-and-prophets foundation, Christ the cornerstone, a dwelling for God by the Spirit.
Add the practice: humility, no selfish ambition, others' interests.
The audience is slaves under earthly masters; include work as for Christ, the inheritance, impartial judgment.
Stray '}'; 'them' means other churches; include the greeting and thanks for growing faith, love and endurance.
